clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. Sabrina presented with a generally cheerful and cooperative affect, facilitating initial engagement in tasks. Observations indicated normotonic muscle tone and full range of motion across major joints. Her attention span was variable, with frequent episodes of distractibility necessitating repeated visual and verbal cues. During structured activities, Sabrina demonstrated engagement, albeit requiring significant external prompting compared to self-directed tasks. Fine motor coordination was observed to be emerging; Sabrina required hand-over-hand assistance to complete tasks necessitating bilateral manipulation, impacting the efficiency of task completion. Behavioral observations noted during testing included mild frustration at times, affecting the validity of standardized test scores, which necessitated adaptation of test administration procedures to accommodate her attentional needs.
